In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the all-trans polyene chain in red coral is 9 – 11 C = = C in length.
the all-trans polyene chain in the red coral pigment contains at least 10 C = = C double bonds, which is in agreement with the previously published data.
the all-cis polyene pigment in the red coral is a chain of 12 conjugated carbon–carbon double units, and the all-trans polyene is a chain of at least 9 conjugated carbon– carbon double units.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the calculated structural parameters for all-trans and cis polyenes converge to limiting values with increasing chain length and that the calculated ν(C – C) and, in particular, ν(C = C) wavenumures can be corrected to give reliable values that can be used to estimate the number of conjugated double bonds present in a polyene.
the calculated structural and vibrational data for polyenes can be used for the identification of the presence of these compounds and their number of carbon–carbon double bounds in natural products.
the BLYP/6311++G** method provides a good compromise between the computational cost and accuracy of calculated geometries and vibrational frequencies for all-trans polyenes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structural and vibratioal parameters of polyenes are not sensitive to their size, and the same parameters can be used to describe all-trans polyenes containing up 100 C =  C units.
the structural parameters and vibrational wavenumbers of polyenes are not affected by the length of the conjugated chain and are determined by the type of conjugation, i.e. all-trans or all-cis.
